_comment: Rates in USD per token, keyed by EXACT model string including any context suffix such as [1m] -- long-context pricing differs and must not be normalised away. Jev bills input only; output is free.
_cache_write_multiplier_1h_note: A cache write with a 1-HOUR TTL bills at 2x the input rate; the 1.25x above is the 5-MINUTE rate. Which TTL a row used is recorded per row in usage.cache_creation {ephemeral_5m_input_tokens, ephemeral_1h_input_tokens} and must be READ, not inferred from the auth path -- both TTLs occur in this project's own corpus (12,334,854 tokens of 5m writes across 27 sessions; 5,161,696 tokens of 1h writes in one). Source: ccusage#899, $479 / 19% under-reported across ~40,000 records before PR #1221. NOT independently reconciled here: no session in this corpus that used 1h writes has written a cost-state line, so 2.0 is taken from the published rate card and the 1.25x figure is the only one verified against first-party accounting (see _verification).
_verification: Haiku 4.5 and Sonnet 5 rates reproduce Claude Code's own cost-state.costUSD exactly on a real transcript, once web search is billed at $0.01/request -- see FINDINGS.md Appendix B. The Jev rate is confirmed against the gateway's own /v1/models metadata: pricing.input 4.2e-8, pricing.output 0 -- see FINDINGS.md Appendix A.

typesafe-ai/jev.note: Gateway reports context_window 32000 (not the 64000 some secondary sources give) and max_tokens 0 -- type 'evaluation', it cannot generate text.

claude-opus-4-7._derivation: NOT guessed and NOT substring-matched from 'opus' -- that is claude-spend#31's 437% over-report. Solved from first-party accounting: 5e-06/2.5e-05 is the unique rate pair that reproduces cost-state.modelUsage['claude-opus-4-7'].costUSD to the cent in all 28 sessions of this project that report one, with cache writes at 1.25x and cache reads at 0.10x. Worked example, session 0982af7b: in 9, out 4969, cache write 49379, cache read 126594 -> 0.49618575, against a reported 0.49618575. JEV-49.

claude-opus-5[1m].note: The [1m] suffix means the 1M context window is ENABLED, not that every request was billed at the long-context premium -- Claude Code applies premium pricing per request, above a threshold. A flat 5.00 rate therefore under-reports this model by a few percent on long sessions. The reconciliation delta is published rather than tuned away.

claude-fable-5-1.note: UNVERIFIED against cost-state. More expensive than Opus on input and output, but cache reads are half Opus's in absolute terms ($0.25 vs $0.50/MTok). Fable is not a cheaper tier -- it is a DIFFERENTLY SHAPED one, cheaper only on cache-heavy terse turns.

_cache_read_multiplier_note: cache_read_multiplier is a GLOBAL 0.10, verified empirically against Claude Code's own cost-state for Haiku 4.5 and Sonnet 5 (exact to the cent). Fable 5.1 is reported to break this: $0.25/MTok cache read against a $10/MTok input rate is 2.5%, not 10%. That is UNVERIFIED -- it comes from documentation, not from reconciliation against cost-state as the others were. Until a real Fable session can be reconciled, treat Fable cost figures as provisional. Per-model cache_read override below takes precedence over the global when present.
